o1.biggest_strength: Gives a clear verdict per ad set with rupee logic, relaunches the paused winner first, and splits out women 25-34 instead of killing the ad set.
o1.biggest_mistake: The break-even math is applied inconsistently (uses ₹394 as 'break-even on Meta's own count' while calling ₹282 the safe/UTM line), so the per-ad-set lines and losses don't cleanly trace to one model.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the working for each ad set's break-even line (order value, COD/RTO, and the 72% haircut) so the scale/hold/fix/cut calls are unarguable.

o2.biggest_strength: Ties every decision to a per-ad-set break-even line built from its own COD/RTO mix and the 72% UTM gap, and calls out the unspent ₹1,30,400 rather than forcing the full budget out.
o2.biggest_mistake: Slightly heavier and more number-dense than a grade-7 reader wants, and the reserve ladder math is dense enough to slow a Monday-morning decision.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Trim to the decisions and one-line reasons, keeping the per-ad-set lines, so the team can act without wading through the projection detail.

reason: Both follow the owner's signals, but Output 2 builds each ad set's line from its own COD/RTO mix and refuses to spend money that loses, which is exactly how this owner thinks. Output 1 is clear and right on the big calls but its break-even logic wobbles between ₹282 and ₹394.
